title: Hubble Reveals Galactic History Through Messier 30 Globular Cluster
content:
A new NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image highlights the globular star cluster Messier 30, also known as NGC 7099, to illustrate lessons in galactic history. Named after French astronomer Charles Messier, who cataloged the object in the early days of telescoping, M30 is located approximately 27,500 light-years away in the constellation Capricornus. The image serves as a visual record of the cluster, which consists of tens of thousands to millions of stars arranged in a roughly spherical grouping.

Globular clusters are ancient celestial objects, with estimated ages ranging from 11.5 to 13.5 billion years, making them nearly as old as the universe. These clusters typically reside in the galactic halo, orbiting on the outskirts of galaxies. The Milky Way contains at least 150 such clusters, with the nearest located about 6,000 light-years from Earth. Because of their age, globular clusters act as time capsules that preserve the original chemistry of the young galaxy, offering astronomers clues about how the Milky Way developed.

Historical research has relied on these clusters to map the galaxy. More than a century ago, astronomer Harlow Shapley used observations of variable stars to determine that the Sun is not at the center of the galaxy and that the galactic center lies toward the constellation Sagittarius. Although his distance measurements were incorrect, leading him to conclude the galaxy was twice its actual size, his work fundamentally shifted understanding of the Sun’s position. Today, astronomers continue to use globular clusters to study galactic evolution, noting that some clusters, including M30, orbit in the opposite direction of the galaxy’s spin. This suggests that these clusters may have been captured by the Milky Way in the distant past rather than forming within it.

Hubble has observed M30 through multiple programs to study its stellar populations. A previous program led by Sarajedini used the Advanced Camera for Surveys to survey dozens of Milky Way globular clusters in red and near-infrared light, revealing stars with masses as low as 20% of the Sun’s. A more recent program led by Piotto utilized the Wide Field Camera 3 with three filters capturing bluer light to investigate “blue straggler” stars and multiple stellar populations within the clusters.

The featured image combines data from three distinct observing programs, including a recent ACS program led by Libralato that tracked the movement of different star populations over 15 years. By utilizing Hubble’s longevity and ability to discern small details, this program analyzed how stars moved since the initial observations. The final image incorporates ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared wavelengths, providing a comprehensive view that helps scientists understand the formation and evolution of these stellar groups.
summary: Hubble Reveals Galactic History Through Messier 30 Globular Cluster.

title: Rivet Launches Fast, Scalable Agent Orchestrator Using S3
content:
Nathan and Nicholas from Rivet announced the public launch of their new agent orchestration platform on Hacker News. Rivet, a YC F25 startup, is described as a fast, high‑density, and scalable orchestrator that uses the actor model to run agentic workloads. Instead of launching a heavyweight sandbox for each agent, Rivet assigns a lightweight actor backed by Amazon S3. Each actor maintains a long‑lived process for extended agent turns, keeps in‑memory state for context, hosts a WebSocket server for multiplayer interactions, and uses durable SQLite storage that is persisted to S3. Idle actors can hibernate, and the platform offers a similar model to Cloudflare Durable Objects while remaining open source and self‑hostable.

The founders explain that their experience building multiplayer game infrastructure—specifically for titles such as Diep and Krunker—led them to develop Rivet Actors. The game servers required high‑throughput matchmaking, real‑time player messaging, and rapid scaling. PostgreSQL could not keep up with the throughput, so the team initially used Lua scripts on top of Redis, which proved hard to maintain. By extending their orchestrator to support lightweight actors, they were able to serve tens of millions of monthly active users. The shift to actors also addressed inefficiencies of sandboxed agents: a baseline actor uses 72 KB of memory versus 512 MB for a minimal sandbox, and actors start in 4.9 ms at the 99th percentile compared to 1.7 seconds for sandboxes.

Rivet’s architecture relies on S3 for durable storage while maintaining SSD‑like speeds. The platform was originally built on FoundationDB, but the volume of data—large session transcripts, agent artifacts, and full POSIX filesystems—outgrew PostgreSQL and made idle SSDs costly. Switching to S3 reduced storage costs by roughly tenfold compared to EBS gp3. To keep write latency low, writes to an actor’s SQLite database are acknowledged once SSDs in two of three availability zones have the data, then batched to S3 in the background. Reads first consult the SSD cache and fall back to S3 if necessary, yielding durable write latency of 1.07 ms (p99), read latency of 1.36 ms (p99), and 138 ms for object‑storage reads (p99).

Deployment options are designed for flexibility. A single Rust binary, with S3 as the only dependency, allows self‑hosting. Rivet Cloud offers dedicated clusters on AWS or GCP in any region, while a Bring‑Your‑Own‑Cloud (BYOC) model lets users deploy within their own VPC without operating the service. The platform runs identically in local development and production, supporting agent development in TypeScript or Rust. Out‑of‑the‑box features include agents (Pi Durable), workflows, real‑time multiplayer, AI‑generated code execution, Durable Streams, and integrations with tools such as Vercel’s Eve and Turso.

For those interested in testing the system, Rivet provides quick‑start guides and a skills package that can be installed with `npx skills add rivet-dev/skills`. The company encourages feedback on the experience and offers resources such as architecture documentation, benchmarking results, and self‑hosting instructions on its website. The launch post also includes links to the GitHub repository, the architecture overview, and a Hacker News discussion thread.
summary: Rivet Launches Fast, Scalable Agent Orchestrator Using S3.

title: Texas AI boom faces threat after blue wave shifts energy policy
content:
The Download: Texas’s fragile AI boom and energy policy shifts

The latest edition of The Download highlights how Texas’s position as the fastest‑growing data‑center market in the United States is now under pressure. The state has long been the center of Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts, but recent election results could jeopardize that status.

In the November midterms, Democrat James Talarico won the U.S. Senate seat, Gina Hinojosa was elected governor, and Democrats secured control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Campaigns in Texas made data centers a central issue, and the new political alignment may spell trouble for hyperscalers with ambitious plans in the state. The shift also adds to growing anxiety that America’s AI buildout could stall, as the newsletter notes.

Beyond Texas, the midterms have broader implications for U.S. energy policy. Democrats now control both the House and the Senate, but the newsletter cautions that major federal climate and energy legislation is unlikely while Donald Trump remains president. The election outcomes could, however, shape state and local energy decisions, influencing everything from the state grid and data‑center development to renewable energy projects and greenhouse‑gas emissions.

A new piece of legislation, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), is poised to change how the United States builds energy infrastructure. The Senate is set to vote on the bill on November 9. BAAJA proposes to overhaul the slow, complicated process for approving energy projects, potentially speeding up infrastructure development. Some environmental groups, however, oppose the bill or parts of it, according to the newsletter’s coverage.

Together, these developments underscore a period of transition for both Texas’s AI ambitions and the broader U.S. energy landscape. The political shifts in Texas and the federal government, coupled with the pending BAAJA vote, could reshape the future of data‑center growth and energy infrastructure across the country.
summary: Texas was the fastest-growing data center market, but the 2026 blue wave—Democrats winning the Senate seat, the governorship, and the Texas House—made data centers a central campaign issue, threatening the state's AI boom. The new Democratic majority also shifts energy policy, potentially affecting state grid, renewable energy, and permitting for AI-related infrastructure.

title: FAA to replace floppy disks with new Enterprise Information Display System
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration is preparing to retire the 3.5‑inch magnetic floppy disks that still run critical portions of U.S. airspace. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced on Thursday that the agency will replace the legacy technology with a new digital platform.

The rollout will introduce the Enterprise‑Information Display System (E‑IDS), which is slated to replace four existing setups across more than 400 air‑traffic‑control facilities. According to the announcement, E‑IDS will consolidate real‑time weather alerts, equipment‑outage notices, restricted‑airspace changes and pilot reports onto a modern digital display.

A photograph taken by Kevin Carter of Getty Images shows the San Diego International Airport control tower on May 27, illustrating the environment in which the upgrade will take place. The transition marks the FAA’s effort to move away from floppy‑disk‑based systems toward contemporary information‑display technology.
summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced that the FAA will stop using 3.5‑inch magnetic floppy disks. The agency will roll out the Enterprise‑Information Display System (E‑IDS) to replace four legacy setups at more than 400 air‑traffic‑control facilities, aggregating weather alerts, equipment outages, restricted‑airspace changes and pilot reports.

content: Mercedes-Benz provided flights from San Francisco to Malaga, Spain, and accommodation so Ars could drive the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. EA sports-car architecture does a lot of heavy lifting here, constantly adjusting power delivery from the three motors while guiding the Active Ride Control suspension, steering—including up to 6 degrees at the rear axle—and active aerodynamics to deliver the performance AMG customers have come to expect from a vehicle with the Affalterbach badge on the hood. title: Astronauts to finish installing final ISS solar array in spacewalk
content:
NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk are scheduled to complete the upgrade of the International Space Station’s power system on November 5. The pair will perform a roughly seven-hour spacewalk beginning at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT) to install the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA). The event is available for live viewing starting at 7 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT).

This extravehicular activity marks the second spacewalk in a week for Menon and Kutryk, who installed the seventh iROSA during an excursion on October 29. That previous mission was the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the ISS and the first EVA for a Canadian astronaut since 2019. According to NASA officials, today’s installation will conclude a process that began in June 2021 to increase the station’s power-generating capacity from 160 kilowatts to approximately 215 kilowatts, representing a boost of about 30%.

Currently, Menon and Kutryk are sharing the station with five other crew members: NASA astronauts Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins, and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina, and Sergey Teteryatnikov. Delaney, Kutryk, Teteryatnikov, and Watkins arrived on October 1 via the SpaceX Crew-13 mission, while Dubrov, Kikina, and Menon arrived in mid-July aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.
summary: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk will install the final Roll-Out Solar Array during a seven-hour spacewalk. This activity completes a five-year upgrade that increases the station's power capacity from 160 to 215 kilowatts.

title: ‘Whitewater is ephemeral. That’s why we chase it’: Nouria Newman on the risk and thrill of extreme kayaking
content:
French professional kayaker Nouria Newman recently attempted to paddle the Klinaklini River in north-western British Columbia, a waterway described as one of the most elusive in the world. While Newman had initially checked the water gauge and found the levels to be good, overnight rain caused water flows to double. This sudden change turned the Class V lower gorge into a dangerous obstacle, complicating her plans to navigate the river.

The Klinaklini River presents a significant challenge to paddlers. Of the three groups that previously attempted to paddle the full 125 miles to the Pacific, only one was successful. Newman, whose early career was defined by competition success, has since turned to wild rivers and waterfall drops. She aimed to be the second person to successfully complete the full route, seeking the risk and thrill associated with extreme kayaking.
summary: ‘Whitewater is ephemeral. That’s why we chase it’: Nouria Newman on the risk and thrill of extreme kayaking.

title: UEFA faces pressure over Sevastopol's promotion to Russian third tier
content:
FC Sevastopol, a club based in Crimea, has won promotion to Russia’s professional third tier, creating a potential political flashpoint for football governing bodies. The team was declared champions of group one in the Football National League (FNL) 2B, effectively Russia’s fourth division, last month. They are believed to have applied for a licence to compete in the level above, FNL 2A.

This development presents a decisive test for Uefa and Fifa regarding their stance on the integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory. If Sevastopol is granted a licence and proceeds to FNL 2A, it would constitute a clear violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from participating in competitions organized by the Russian Football Union (RFU).

The situation places severe pressure on Uefa to extend sanctions against Russia, which is currently banned from competing in international tournaments. The outcome of the licensing process will determine whether the governing bodies enforce their existing regulations amidst the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.
summary: FC Sevastopol won promotion to Russia's professional third tier, a move that would violate UEFA rules prohibiting Crimean clubs from playing in Russian competitions. UEFA and FIFA face a decisive test regarding their willingness to extend sanctions against the Russian Football Union.

title: Australian F1 World Champion Alan Jones Dies Aged 80
content:

title: Sherrock Wins £501,000 Prize in Netflix Darts Special Over Luke Littler
content: Decades of professionalism, investment and industrialised training methods have rendered the gulf between the sporting gods and mortals virtually unbridgeable “She walked in here a hairdresser from Milton Keynes – and walks out £501,000 richer!” Gary Lineker announced at the conclusion of Netflix’s Beat Luke Littler on Friday night. Which, while strictly accurate as a description of the winner Fallon Sherrock, arguably fell some way short of providing the full picture. “She walked in wearing socks – and walks out £501,000 richer!” “She walked in here a vertebrate mammal – and walks out £501,000 richer!” I mean, if we’re just reciting facts without context here. Because while Sherrock may still theoretically be qualified to cut hair, much of her past decade has been spent on darts: playing darts, practising darts, travelling to and from darts, promoting her darts career. Though she may never have held a Professional Darts Corporation tour card, she is – by any sane definition of the term – a professional darts player. Indeed, as a result of her historic run to the third round of the world championship at Alexandra Palace in late 2019, she may still be the second most famous darts player in the country, after Littler himself.
summary: Gary Lineker announced that Fallon Sherrock walked in as a hairdresser from Milton Keynes and walked out £501,000 richer after winning Netflix’s Beat Luke Littler. Sherrock, a professional darts player, is noted for her historic run to the third round of the 2019 world championship at Alexandra Palace.

title: World's wettest rainstorms become shorter and more intense, study finds
content:
A new study reveals that the world’s wettest rainstorms, which account for approximately half of global annual rainfall, are becoming shorter in duration and fewer in number. This shift compresses the same volume of rain into quicker, more extreme events, carrying significant implications for both flood and drought risks.

Researchers Chiyuan Miao and colleagues from Beijing Normal University in China analyzed daily measurements from over 19,000 global rain gauges between 1980 and 2022. Their findings indicate that an average of half the world’s rainfall now falls during roughly nine multi-day storms, delivered over a cumulative period of about 28 days.

The research projects the impact of climate breakdown on four key groups of marine life essential for maintaining ocean ecosystems in the region.

The scientists’ findings challenge the assumption that marine biodiversity in middle latitudes, such as the UK, is likely to increase across the board. Instead, the report suggests that warming waters could fundamentally reshape these marine ecosystems.

title: Centuries-old cemetery links climate shocks to Industrial Revolution disease
content:
Scientists have used a centuries‑old cemetery in England to connect climate shocks with disease outbreaks that occurred during the Industrial Revolution.  

During the period from roughly 1760 to 1840, England’s shift from a farming‑based economy to an industrial one brought pollution, harsh working conditions, inadequate housing and limited sunlight, all of which drove disease. Rickets, a condition in which a child’s skeleton fails to mineralize properly, was common. While urbanization, latitude and socioeconomic status were traditionally seen as the main drivers, climate has largely been overlooked.
summary: Scientists used a centuries-old cemetery to link climate shocks to disease during England's Industrial Revolution. The study highlights that pollution, harsh working conditions, inadequate housing, and limited sunlight contributed to widespread rickets among children.

title: Archaeologist says Verica who urged Claudius’s AD43 invasion may have been a queen
content:
A controversial claim has emerged from Bournemouth University, where Dr Miles Russell, director of archaeological fieldwork, argues that the British ruler who persuaded Emperor Claudius to launch the AD 43 invasion was not a king but a queen. Russell’s conclusion challenges the long‑held view that Verica was a male monarch.

The AD 43 landing of Roman troops under Claudius at Kent marked a turning point in British history. If Russell’s theory that Verica was a woman is accepted, it could offer a new perspective on the early Roman–British relationship and the roles of female leaders in that era.
summary: Dr Miles Russell, director of archaeological fieldwork at Bournemouth University, claims the British ruler Verica, traditionally called a king, may have been a queen who persuaded Emperor Claudius to launch the AD43 invasion of Britain. The theory is presented as controversial and could reshape interpretations of early British history.

title: US prosecutors drop charges against Russian scientist detained over frog embryos
content:
Federal prosecutors have dropped all criminal charges against Russian scientist Kseniia Petrova, 31, who had spent four months in immigration detention after flying into Boston with frog embryos intended for cancer research at Harvard Medical School.

Petrova was arrested in March 2025 after returning from a vacation in France, where she visited a laboratory that specializes in cutting extremely thin sections of frog embryos. During that visit she obtained a package of samples for her research back in the US. She had feared deportation to Russia.
summary: US prosecutors drop charges against Russian scientist detained over frog embryos.

title: Guardian podcast examines if ‘ferritin face’ can diagnose iron deficiency
content:
Social media is flooded with claims that iron deficiency can be spotted in the mirror by dark circles, hair breakage and dry skin. The Guardian podcast “Ferritin face” asks whether these so‑called “ferritin face” signs are real or simply myth.

In the episode, Madeleine Finlay talks with journalist Ian Sample about why many people struggle to maintain adequate iron levels, how low iron can actually be diagnosed, and the most effective ways to correct a deficiency.

The discussion is supported by experts Hal Drakesmith, professor of iron biology at Oxford University, and Dr Sue Pavord, consultant haematologist at Oxford University Hospitals and associate senior lecturer in clinical medicine at St Edmund Hall.
summary: Social media is awash with claims iron deficiency can be identified in the mirror by dark circles, breaking hair and dry skin. But is ‘ferritin face’ real?

title: Swapping from dairy to plant-based milk, cheese and yoghurt ‘could lead to micronutrient deficiencies’
content:
A new study indicates that switching from dairy to plant-based alternatives for milk, cheese, and yoghurt may cause deficiencies in essential micronutrients. Researchers identified young people and women as being at the highest risk for these nutritional shortfalls. The study highlights that even partial shifts to vegan substitutes, which are frequently based on soya, almonds, or oats, can result in reduced intake of iodine, calcium, riboflavin, and vitamin B12 if the products are not fortified.

In response to these findings, scientists are calling for specific interventions to address the nutritional gap. They have urged that vegan products be fortified with iodine in particular to prevent these deficiencies among vulnerable populations.
summary: Swapping from dairy to plant-based milk, cheese and yoghurt ‘could lead to micronutrient deficiencies’.

title: NASA unveils X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft for advanced flight research
content: Generated image of NASA’s new X-70 Fractal experimental aircraft, a crewed, rapidly reconfigurable research platform for advanced aviation technologies. On Wednesday, NASA unveiled its newest experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, during the UP. Summit at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. This high-performance, highly adaptable research platform is designed to accelerate the development and testing of advanced aviation technologies. The crewed X-70 features advanced, rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology that will allow NASA to explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight. The aircraft can also accommodate up to 2,000 pounds of experimental payloads in internal and external locations, enabling a wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities. “The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next. We expect her first flight under the NASA banner within the next two years, and X-70 is just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics. This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly.” The X-70 Fractal has a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds and is designed to cruise at Mach.75, reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet, and provide an operational range exceeding about 1,726 miles (1,500 nautical miles). These capabilities will enable NASA to conduct demanding flight research across a broad range of operating conditions. “For decades, NASA Aeronautics has used X-planes to develop technologies that advance aviation,” said Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. “It’s exciting to bring on another X-plane to accelerate and drive aeronautics research.” The X-70 joins a storied legacy of experimental aircraft that have helped establish America’s leadership in aviation. From the Bell X-1, which first broke the sound barrier in 1947, to the X-15 hypersonic research aircraft and today’s X-59 quiet supersonic demonstrator, NASA has spent decades pushing the boundaries of flight. With the X-70, NASA will expand its capacity to conduct experimental flight research, accelerate the testing of emerging technologies, and advance the next generation of American aviation. title: Cyprus's Akrotiri Peninsula: Ophiolite Island, Seasonal Lake, Flamingo Decline
content:
NASA Earth Observatory recently published a feature detailing the geological and biological history of Cyprus, centered on imagery captured by the Landsat 8 Operational Land Imager on October 10, 2026. The images focus on the Akrotiri Peninsula, the southernmost tip of the island, where seasonal rains had begun to fill the Akrotiri Salt Lake. The article explains that Cyprus began forming approximately 90 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period, when molten rock from the seafloor solidified to create new oceanic crust. Tectonic forces later uplifted portions of this rock, forming a rugged island composed of ophiolite, a green, mottled stone often compared to snake skin. Remnants of this ancient formation are visible in the dark rocks of the Troodos Mountains.

During the Miocene, younger layers of chalk, limestone, and other marine sediments accumulated around the original island. These materials eventually formed a second, smaller island to the south during a later period of geologic uplift. Sediments from rivers and marine sources combined to create deltas and two land bridges, known as tombolos, which joined the landmasses into the current Akrotiri Peninsula. The westerly Kouris River tombolo formed first, developing about 50,000 years ago from river-deposited gravels and sands. The eastern tombolo extended southward from the main island, cutting off the Mediterranean Sea to form the coastal lagoon only within the past 2,000 years, according to geologists.

The Akrotiri Salt Lake, situated between the two tombolos, experiences significant seasonal water level changes, typically filling in late autumn and winter before drying out in summer. Historically, the influx of winter water attracted large populations of overwintering flamingos, averaging about 4,000 birds. The flamingos feed on fairy shrimp, which contain carotenoids responsible for the birds’ pink coloration. However, news reports indicate that the wintering flamingo population has declined sharply in recent years, plummeting to 30 birds in 2025.

The article also highlights the island’s reputation for snakes and cats. In antiquity, Cyprus was known as Ophiousa, or “land of snakes,” likely due to a robust population of blunt-nosed vipers. Legend states that during a fourth-century drought, Roman Empress Helena ordered shiploads of cats from Egypt to control the venomous reptiles. These cats were first released in the southeastern part of the Akrotiri Peninsula, an area known as Cape Gata, or Cape Cat in Greek. Today, the Holy Monastery of St. Nicholas of the Cats remains in this area, where a handful of nuns care for hundreds of cats.

Current statistics indicate that Cyprus has as many cats as people, with more than one million felines on the island. The NASA Earth Observatory story, written by Adam Voiland and featuring images by Michala Garrison, uses this combination of geological history and wildlife dynamics to illustrate the unique environmental characteristics of the Akrotiri Peninsula.
summary: Cyprus's Akrotiri Peninsula: Ophiolite Island, Seasonal Lake, Flamingo Decline.

content: A new United Kingdom law slated to take effect will prohibit simulated incest and certain depictions of oral sex. Adult content creators and free‑speech advocates have voiced alarm about the measure, warning it could represent an unprecedented level of sex censorship.

title: Nintendo designers aimed for elegance in Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake
content:
Nintendo’s Ocarina of Time remake for the Switch 2 blends the classic N64 experience with contemporary visuals and gameplay, preserving the original’s core while adding modern graphics.  

The project is led by producers Eiji Aonuma—former director of the original game and current steward of the franchise at Nintendo—and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, best known for directing Breath of the Wild and its sequel.  The team also includes a number of younger developers, some of whom had never played the original title.
summary: The Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2 smashes together the past and present. The game retains much of the original N64 experience while updating it with modern graphics and gameplay that make it feel contemporary.

title: Silicon Valley billionaires pictured with Trump face scrutiny from Democratic Congress
content: Democrats’ success was helped by popular anger over tech, AI and the super rich – life for billionaires could become much more difficult The photo of Silicon Valley centi-billionaires at Donald Trump’s inauguration – Musk, Bezos, and Zuckerberg, front row and side by side – now looks like a hitlist for a blue Congress hellbent on making life difficult for billionaires. The picture symbolized at the time the bending of the knee by the richest men in the world to its most powerful, a symbiosis of the ultra-rich. Already unfathomably wealthy, Silicon Valley tycoons believed a Maga-sized public shift to the right would enrich them even more. It did. For several years, while Trump seemed an everlasting kingmaker and AI’s expansion seemed unstoppable, their fortunes ballooned to values beyond comprehension. Elon Musk’s surpassed $1tn.
summary: Silicon Valley billionaires pictured with Trump face scrutiny from Democratic Congress.

content: CERN scientists have reported evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay observed with the Large Hadron Collider. The decay, predicted to happen only once in every 10 billion cases, provides researchers with a new avenue for probing the subatomic world.

content: Volunteers in New Zealand are confronting a mass stranding of pilot whales along the Wairarapa coast near Cape Palliser. While they have managed to return at least 14 whales to the sea, many others have been found dead along the remote shoreline. The effort highlights the ongoing challenge of rescuing the stranded cetaceans.

title: Trump Proclaims American Space Superiority in Election Night Declaration
content:
On November 3, President Trump issued the "American Declaration of Freedom in Space," a proclamation asserting that space is the "province of all humans" open for exploration. The document declares the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system under United States laws, positioning the U.S. as the leader of humanity’s expansion into the cosmos. While the proclamation invokes the nation’s "frontier spirit" and cites Apollo 11 astronauts and robotic Mars rovers as examples of American leadership, it does not introduce new funding, programs, or policy directives.

The declaration emphasizes the administration’s goals for NASA’s Artemis program, which aims to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 and eventually send them to Mars. It highlights the success of the Artemis II mission in April, which carried four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon, setting a record for the farthest humans have traveled from Earth. According to the proclamation, the follow-up Artemis III mission is scheduled to launch in the summer of 2027 to test rendezvous and docking operations between the Orion spacecraft and commercial lunar landers. Artemis IV is targeted for 2028 as the program’s first lunar landing mission, with a December 2025 executive order reaffirming the goal of deploying initial elements for a permanent lunar outpost by 2030.

The document pledges that the United States will carry values of faith, freedom, and individual liberty into an interplanetary civilization, stating that "American space superiority for all eternity" will be ensured by the country’s flourishing commercial space sector. Although the proclamation does not establish new NASA programs or allocate additional funding, its language echoes principles from the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which guarantees freedom of exploration while prohibiting national sovereignty claims on other planets.
summary: President Trump issued a declaration yesterday (Nov. 3), proclaiming space open to all humanity for exploration, and the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system according to United States laws.

title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
content:
On November 4, 2015, the United States Air Force attempted a debut launch of the experimental Super Strypi rocket from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The rail-launched vehicle was designed to carry small payloads into orbit, marking a modern evolution of the 1960s Strypi sounding rocket. The mission intended to place 13 tiny satellites, known as cubesats, into space, but the launch failed less than a minute after liftoff.

The rocket lifted off at approximately 9:45 p.m. local time on November 3, 2015, but quickly spun out of control and crashed. The failure likely resulted from a problem with the first-stage motor and destroyed all 13 cubesats aboard. The primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, also nicknamed HiakaSat, which was built by engineers at the University of Hawaii for the Air Force to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment. The remaining 12 payloads included eight cubesats for NASA’s Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission and four additional university payloads.

Super Strypi was a three-stage rocket powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, designed to reach orbit rather than suborbital trajectories. The Air Force hoped the system would serve as a tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs, capable of launching up to 300 kilograms of payload for $15 million per mission. Following the 2015 failure, the program never recovered, and the Air Force did not attempt another launch with this rocket.

In the years since the failure, the U.S. Space Force has shifted its strategy for fast-turnaround launch support to commercial companies. In June of this year, the Space Force partnered with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with only 17 hours of notice, setting a new record for short-turnaround launch response.
summary: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii.

title: Bournemouth's calm approach after Marco Rose's winless start is paying off
content:
Bournemouth’s decision to remain calm following a difficult start to the Premier League season is beginning to pay off. The club’s head coach, Marco Rose, failed to secure a victory in his first six league matches, recording three defeats and three draws. This initial lack of success, combined with the summer departure of his predecessor, Andoni Iraola, led to media speculation regarding Rose’s future and concern among supporters.

However, the club maintained a positive and steady approach, recognizing that new tactical methods often require time to produce results. Bournemouth fans drew parallels to Iraola’s tenure, noting that he also did not win any of his first nine Premier League games upon taking charge. content:

content:
Veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett is set to move from the Arizona Cardinals to the Baltimore Ravens, according to a source with knowledge of the deal who spoke to the Associated Press on Wednesday. content:

The Czech champions extended their winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history to 23 matches, equalling the record held by AEK Athens and FCSB. Despite this, Slavia Prague mounted a spirited late comeback that tested Arsenal’s defense.

summary: Viktor Gyökeres scored as Arsenal defeated Slavia Prague, a result that left the Czech team with a 23-match winless streak in European Cup and Champions League history. title: VIB and KU Leuven find ASPM mutations disrupt neural stem cells, causing microcephaly
content:
Researchers at VIB and KU Leuven have identified how mutations in the ASPM gene disrupt the development of neural stem cells essential for human brain growth. This disruption causes microcephaly, a condition defined by an abnormally small brain and head, which is frequently accompanied by intellectual disability. The findings, published in Developmental Cell, clarify the specific mechanisms behind this developmental failure.

The study also highlights how variations in brain development render humans more susceptible to certain genetic conditions than other mammals. By uncovering these distinct developmental pathways, the research provides insight into the unique vulnerability of the human brain to ASPM gene mutations.
summary: Researchers at VIB and KU Leuven have uncovered how mutations in the ASPM gene disrupt the development of neural stem cells that help the human brain grow. content:
Brazil’s "Dirty List," a public registry identifying employers who violated anti-slavery laws, remains a central tool in the country’s fight against forced labor. Major meatpackers have committed to sustainable sourcing by refusing to buy cattle directly from ranchers named on this list. However, new research indicates that these safeguards are being circumvented. Ranchers on the list are rerouting their cattle through intermediaries, effectively bypassing the direct purchase restrictions.

This practice allows cattle associated with forced labor to continue moving through domestic and international beef and leather supply chains. The findings suggest that the current sourcing commitments are insufficient to prevent the exploitation of workers, as the use of middlemen obscures the origin of the livestock from the meatpackers.

title: Gauge open-sources CLI to recursively improve docs for coding agents
content:
Evan from Gauge has announced the open-sourcing of a command-line interface (CLI) designed to recursively improve documentation for coding agents. The tool includes a local execution backend, allowing users to try it without creating an account. An explainer video is available to demonstrate the functionality, and the project is hosted on GitHub with installation instructions provided via npm.

The CLI operates on a "hillclimbing loop" designed to optimize agent-facing surfaces such as documentation, Skills, and CLIs. The process involves setting up tasks for coding agents, running those tasks, and analyzing session transcripts to identify friction or failures. Users then create variants of their documentation to resolve these issues and re-run the tasks with the new variants injected transparently at the same hostname. This cycle repeats until a variant successfully resolves the identified problems.

The system’s architecture consists of two main components: virtual machines and a network gateway. The VMs are designed to be highly privileged to accurately represent developers' coding agents, typically containing the agent harness, language toolchains, and a git repository. The network gateway terminates TLS connections and swaps in documentation variants while handling credential replacement. This ensures that agents see placeholders for credentials and cannot exfiltrate keys. For local execution, the CLI uses Docker containers for VMs and runs mitmproxy in a sidecar container for each session to manage the network gateway.

Gauge stated that they began two years ago building open-source developer tools, including Tach, before pivoting to AI Search optimization and now focusing on the intersection of both fields. The team noted that devtool companies they worked with were the first to ask how to optimize for Claude Code and Codex. The CLI provides primitives for documentation, developer relations, and engineering teams to measure and improve how coding agents utilize their products.

The team has used the hillclimbing loop internally to fix issues such as mistaken pricing, inaccurate product limitations, and repeated workarounds. They identified that coding agents incorrectly reported Gauge only supported Claude Code and Codex, traced this to specific web pages, and corrected the documentation to include support for Pi, OpenCode, and Antigravity. Additionally, Gauge assisted Clerk in shifting coding agents from a legacy "keyless" mode to a new "clerk init" command. After validating a pre-release change to SDK error messages using the tool, Clerk observed a threefold increase in coding agents using the "clerk init" command post-deployment.

The developers argue that the static nature of AI models enables closed-loop optimization for software products, as the same agent can be simulated repeatedly in a high-fidelity testing environment. They emphasize that achieving optimal results requires high-quality analysis to find generalizable friction and paired experiments that vary only the content to measure downstream behavioral changes. The post invites feedback from the Hacker News community on whether this approach improves upon DIY or in-house solutions and what changes might be necessary.
summary: Gauge has open-sourced a CLI that uses a hillclimbing loop to analyze session transcripts and create doc variants to resolve coding agent friction. The tool includes a local execution backend using Docker containers and a network gateway to transparently swap in documentation variants during testing.

content:
The Verge’s Allison Johnson shares her experience adopting a phone grip, comparing the initial attraction to finding a great recipe. content:
Qualcomm is pivoting toward the AI data center market to offset a 20 percent decline in smartphone sales compared to 2025. content:
Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) is seeking to expand the Republican majority on the Federal Communications Commission before Democrats assume control of the Senate in January 2027. Cruz announced a nomination hearing for Trump’s FCC nominee, Danielle Thumann Severs, to be held on November 10, shortly after the Republicans’ midterm loss. title: Elon Musk Announces SpaceX HQ Move from California to Texas Starbase
content:
Elon Musk relocated to Texas in 2020, settling outside of Austin following public disputes with California authorities during the COVID-19 pandemic. Over the subsequent six years, he intensified his commitment to the state. In 2021, Musk directed the Starship program toward South Texas, encouraging SpaceX employees to relocate for the company’s future development. That same year, in March, he began using the name Starbase to designate the production and launch facilities situated near the Rio Grande River.

Musk continued to expand SpaceX’s presence in Texas in 2023 by constructing a massive factory east of Austin. This facility is dedicated to manufacturing customer terminals and other electronics for the Starlink program. In July 2024, he announced that SpaceX would move its corporate headquarters from Hawthorne, California, to Starbase, Texas. Musk cited California’s regulatory and political environment as the primary motivation for this corporate relocation.
summary: Elon Musk moved to Texas in 2020 after disputes with California authorities and focused the Starship program and Starlink factory there. title: Voters Pass 38 of 44 Data Center Restrictions, Slowing Trump’s AI Buildout
content: Donald Trump’s big, rapid American AI buildout now faces a major slowdown as voters in yesterday’s elections overwhelmingly supported candidates and measures that favored increasing restrictions on AI and data centers nationwide. One resource from a polling firm, called Redbud Consulting, tracked data center initiatives on the ballot and reported that out of 44 measures across 10 states seeking to restrict data centers, 38 passed so far. Those measures included dozens of moratoriums and bans. Analysts suggested those won’t impact data centers already under construction or approved through 2027, instead largely impacting future projects planned for 2028. Only one measure passed allowing a data center to proceed. But even that small win represented pushback on the AI industry—requiring data center developers in a North Dakota city to pay for independent reviews and hold public hearings when expanding or proposing projects. In addition to increasing regulations on data centers, voters also backed anti-AI candidates, electing officials vowing crackdowns in key states building out the most data center capacity in the US. title: AMD Q3 Revenue Hits $13.4B as Data Center Sales Double, Gaming Falls
content:
AMD announced third‑quarter revenues of $13.4 billion, a 45 percent increase from the same period last year. The company said its data‑center business nearly doubled, while the gaming segment declined. Chief financial officer Jean Hu noted that AMD expects revenue for the year to be roughly $17 billion, give or take 3 percent, and that the middle point of its guidance represents about 66 percent year‑over‑year growth, largely driven by the acceleration of the data‑center segment.

AMD projects fourth‑quarter revenue to rise another 27 percent from the current quarter’s results. According to Tom’s Hardware, Intel’s fourth‑quarter guidance places revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, meaning that if both companies meet their estimates, AMD would surpass Intel’s revenue for the first time in history.

The data‑center segment grew 97 percent year over year, reaching a record $8.5 billion. AMD attributes this surge to demand for its EPYC line of enterprise server CPUs and the launch of the Instinct MI450 series GPUs. In the client business, sales of AMD Ryzen mobile chips drove growth, with desktop Ryzen processors contributing $2.95 billion in revenue, up 7 percent year over year.
summary: AMD posted third‑quarter revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45 percent year over year, with its data center segment nearly doubling and its gaming segment falling. title: Uranium cubes show German nuclear program lacked sufficient material
content:
A recent study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus has clarified why the Nazi German nuclear program never produced a bomb. The paper, written by a team that included University of Maryland physicist Timothy Koeth, argues that the German effort lacked the necessary uranium and heavy water to build a functioning reactor, despite claims by Werner Heisenberg that they were close to criticality with the B8 pile.

Heisenberg’s 1940s project had focused on a reactor design that, according to the new research, could not reach critical mass without additional fissile material. The paper’s analysis shows that the German supply of uranium and heavy water was insufficient for the design they were pursuing, contradicting Heisenberg’s assertion that only a small amount of extra material was needed.

Koeth’s interest in the topic began in 2013 when a friend gave him a heavy‑metal cube that he immediately identified as one of the uranium cubes used by German scientists. Only fourteen of these cubes are known to exist today. In 2019, Koeth and then‑graduate student Miriam “Mimi” Hiebert documented their search for the cubes’ origins, locating ten of them across the United States.

Among the cubes they found were a German uranium cube in storage at the Smithsonian Institution and another that had circulated through introductory physics courses at Harvard University. These artifacts provide tangible evidence of the German program’s attempts and help explain why the project ultimately failed.
summary: Uranium cubes show German nuclear program lacked sufficient material.

title: Kremlin-linked hackers exploit iOS and Android flaws to infect phones via malicious sites
content:
Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws to target visitors of multiple websites, researchers said Wednesday. The attackers were assessed with “moderate to high confidence” as part of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service. Their attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites. JavaScript injected into the traffic profiled the device, and the final payloads, tailored to the platform, attempted to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi‑Fi passwords and full mobile device data.

The researchers noted that the attackers targeted other sites, many with links to Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine. One of the impersonated sites was america250.org, a domain belonging to a non‑partisan group of lawmakers, business executives, and at least one former member of the Trump administration. The attackers registered america250.holiday and used it as a reverse proxy to america250.org, delivering content from the real site that included malicious JavaScript.

title: Macronix to Stop ROM Chip Production, Impacting Nintendo Switch Cartridges
content: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM, SSDs, and GPUs. Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges. Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance. That could be an issue for Nintendo, which analyst David Gibson notes uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges. That ROM production—which has shrunk 39 percent in the last year and now represents just 5 percent of Macronix's business—is being crowded out by production of more lucrative, in-demand chips like NOR- and NAND-based memory and eMMCs, the company said. With Macronix's production capacity stuck at 25,000 12-inch wafers a month—and $1.2 billion in planned new capacity taking a year or more to spin up—less profitable ROM chips are taking up wafer space that can earn more through other types of chips. Litvinenko’s deathbed image, showing him in intensive care with a defiant gaze, became a global symbol of the regime under Putin. title: William T Vollmann's 3,000‑page novel A Table for Fortune chronicles CIA history
content: This insider’s history of the CIA explores the last 50 years of US foreign policy with granular detail and mordant humour The 250th year of the American experiment seems to invite a reckoning. For a young country, the United States is overblessed – or burdened – with myths about its foundation and how the nation has conducted itself at home and abroad. William T Vollmann’s 3,000-page novel A Table for Fortune is an epic attempt, 15 years in the making, to engage with the US’s past and present at an institutional and a personal level. The four simultaneously published volumes offer both a family story and an insider’s history of the CIA, in order to show the consequences of the quest for liberty and the belief in American exceptionalism. Vollmann’s previous novels have explored the ideological basis of American society, most notably those of the Seven Dreams series, published from 1990 to 2015, which depict the generally disastrous encounters between American settlers and Indigenous peoples. A Table for Fortune continues this project by investigating the last 50 years of US foreign policy, at the heart of which is 9/11, with the book “tracing the roots of that crime in one direction and its poisoned harvest in another”. Though the CIA has been fertile ground for many great American novelists – Don DeLillo, Norman Mailer – Vollmann is perhaps the first to represent the culture and daily activities of the agency in granular detail. His great gambit is to frame this as a dark workplace comedy of minor resentments, sexual tension and office banter. These sections are narrated by the institutional voice of the CIA itself in a relentlessly sardonic tone rife with acronyms, codenames and jargon rendered in multiple fonts. The mordant humour of the narrator, who regards all forms of death and suffering as “ fun ”, has a seductive quality that allows Vollmann to educate the reader about a broad sweep of geopolitical subjects ranging from the Angolan civil war to the interrogation methods of the Stasi, and in doing so chart the hypocrisies and double standards of the agency.
summary: William T Vollmann's 3,000‑page novel A Table for Fortune chronicles CIA history.

title: England Rugby League Players Stuck in Australia a Week After World Cup Exit
content:
England’s men’s rugby league team is experiencing a delayed departure from the Rugby League World Cup in Australia, with some players not returning home until Friday, a week after their campaign concluded. The squad’s early exit was confirmed on Sunday during the Tonga versus Samoa match, after which the team relocated to Sydney. This prolonged stay contrasts with the England women’s team, who departed Australia the morning after their tournament was ended by Samoa.

During their time in Wollongong, the England men’s squad stayed at a hotel overlooking the local beaches, where the scent of seaweed and mist from the bay was common. The coastal location allowed some players to easily access the water and enabled those with family nearby to begin their end-of-season holidays early. Wigan teammates Junior Nsemba and Zach Eckersley spent time riding e-scooters on Cliff Road and strolling along North Beach, activities that may become significant memories of the trip alongside their matches against Tonga, France, and Papua New Guinea.

Despite the scenic surroundings, which included cafes and lilac jacaranda trees, most England players and staff expressed a strong desire to return home. The situation highlights a period of waiting for the squad, who were effectively told to leave the tournament but remained in the country for an extended period. An advertisement outside their North Bay hotel in Wollongong read, “Everything that truly matters is possible,” a sentiment that did not apply to their immediate circumstances as they waited for their final travel arrangements.
summary: England men's rugby league players will not return home until Friday, a week after their early exit from the World Cup in Australia. The squad has moved to Sydney after their campaign ended, while the women's team departed the morning after their loss to Samoa.

content:

content:

The study, which included participation from the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries (IGB), identifies light pollution as one of the fastest-growing and least-regulated environmental changes worldwide. The authors note that this phenomenon disrupts biological processes at all levels, ranging from genes to entire ecosystems, and contributes significantly to global biodiversity loss.

Based on a comprehensive assessment of impacts on organisms in both terrestrial and aquatic environments, the article outlines specific priorities for future research and management. The review aims to address the widespread effects of light pollution on biological systems, providing a framework for understanding its role in environmental degradation.

title: Toothbrush that emits electricity may more effectively prevent gum disease
content:
A novel toothbrush utilizing piezoelectric bristles has demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing dental plaque and gum inflammation compared to conventional products. Developed by researchers led by Yanhui Lu at Peking University in China, the device generates electricity as its bristles bend during brushing. This mechanical action triggers the formation of reactive-oxygen species, molecules that damage bacterial membranes, while the bristles simultaneously remove plaque physically. The innovation addresses the limitation of standard brushing, which often leaves bacteria deep within plaque or between teeth, allowing colonies to regrow rapidly.

The research team created two sets of bristles with varying thicknesses, both of which adhered to Chinese national standards for softness and strength. Laboratory tests confirmed that the bristles produced electric charges under pressure, with the thicker variants showing particularly high electrical generation. The brushes retained their softness and electrical properties after three months of use. In controlled experiments involving simulated brushing movements, the thicker piezoelectric bristles killed approximately 53 per cent of Streptococcus mutans, a bacterium associated with cavities, and 78 per cent of Porphyromonas gingivalis, which contributes to gum disease. In contrast, standard nylon bristles eliminated only 9 per cent and 8 per cent of these bacteria, respectively.

Further testing involved growing plaque from human mouths on cow enamel pieces and brushing them for three minutes. The piezoelectric toothbrushes removed more than 99 per cent of the plaque, whereas conventional nylon brushes removed about 80 per cent. The study also included a clinical trial with 109 adults who had dental plaque and gum inflammation. Participants were randomly assigned to use either the piezoelectric or a nylon toothbrush twice daily for three months. Dental examinations showed that the piezoelectric group experienced reductions of roughly 40 per cent in plaque build-up, gum inflammation, and bleeding, compared to around 15 per cent for the conventional brush group.

Genetic sequencing of dental plaque from the piezoelectric user group indicated a decline in the relative abundance of harmful bacteria and an increase in some potentially beneficial bacteria. Nicholas Jakubovics, a researcher at Newcastle University in the UK who was not involved in the study, described the concept as innovative because the mechanical forces recharge the surface. He noted that any improvement in dental care methods could be beneficial given the widespread nature of oral disease, which affects nearly half the global population. Previous attempts to enhance toothbrushes have included antibacterial metal nanoparticles or battery-dependent ionic currents, but the long-term effectiveness of some of these methods remains uncertain.

The findings were published in the journal Science Advances. Jakubovics emphasized that larger studies are now required to determine whether the toothbrush effectively prevents long-term issues such as cavities and tooth loss. The research highlights a potential advancement in oral hygiene tools by leveraging piezoelectric materials, which have previously been shown to fight bacteria in infected wounds and medical implants.
summary: A new and improved toothbrush could help avoid trips to the dentist Westend61/Alamy A toothbrush that generates electricity may more effectively fight harmful bacteria, while removing plaque, than existing products. The toothbrush uses special bristles that produce electricity as they bend, triggering the formation of molecules that damage bacterial membranes.

title: Hubble Study Finds Dwarf Galaxies Retain Only Small Fraction of Stellar Oxygen
content:
NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope has captured a new image of NGC 4449, a dwarf irregular galaxy featured in the Galaxies Losing Oxygen via Winds (GLOW) study. Released on November 2, 2026, the photograph highlights this specific galaxy as part of a broader investigation into stellar oxygen retention.

Researchers utilized Hubble to examine 37 nearby dwarf galaxies, defined as small systems containing thousands to hundreds of millions of stars. The study revealed that these galaxies retain only a small fraction of the oxygen produced by their stars, leaving much of the expected oxygen missing. This finding underscores a significant cosmic mystery regarding how dwarf galaxies manage their elemental composition.
summary: Researchers using NASA's Hubble Space Telescope studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies and found that much of the expected oxygen is missing. The study, known as GLOW, revealed that these small galaxies can hold onto only a small fraction of the oxygen made by their stars.

title: NASA awards Ka-band satellite relay contracts to Astranis, Global Enterprise, Viasat
content:
NASA announced on Wednesday that it has awarded contracts to three companies to develop Ka‑band space relay capability concepts that are compatible with current missions in space. The selected firms will design solutions that maintain service continuity for existing spacecraft without requiring modifications to their onboard systems. The work is intended to deliver end‑to‑end solutions—including space, ground, launch, operations, and integration elements—as part of NASA’s broader commercial marketplace strategy.

The awards are firm‑fixed‑price contracts issued under the Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships‑3 Broad Agency Announcement Appendix E. NASA retains the option to provide additional funding, up to the award limit, to advance the projects from initial concept development and risk reduction to an in‑orbit flight demonstration. The initial period of performance runs from November 4 through May 3, 2027, with priced options that could extend the work through 2029.

The contract awardees and their maximum potential values, inclusive of all future options, are: Astranis Space Technologies Corp. for $264.3 million; Global Enterprise Solutions Inc. for $340.4 million; and Viasat Inc. for $460.9 million. These contracts are facilitated through NASA’s SCaN (Space Communications and Navigation) program’s Communications Services Project.

The work supports NASA’s decision to gradually retire the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite fleet and adopt commercial services for future missions. Ka‑band services are also required to support select in‑orbit missions that cannot feasibly modify flight hardware or transition to non‑compatible commercial services. For additional information, visit https://go.Nasa.gov/4iVfeVB.
summary: NASA awards Ka-band satellite relay contracts to Astranis, Global Enterprise, Viasat.

title: Laura Bohn discovers opioid alternative SR‑17018 that avoids respiratory depression
content:
Laura Bohn, senior associate vice president of research at University of South Florida Health, was tasked in 2012 with finding safer pain‑management drugs as the opioid crisis shifted from prescription pills to heroin. The National Institute on Drug Abuse funded her work.

In 2017 Bohn and colleagues published in the journal Cell that several compounds, including a promising one named SR‑17018, could relieve pain in mice without causing respiratory depression—a common cause of opioid‑related death. The study highlighted SR‑17018’s potential to reduce pain without the life‑threatening breathing suppression seen with many opioids.

The team filed a patent on SR‑17018 and discovered that mice treated with the chemical did not develop a high tolerance. Additionally, mice already dependent on morphine could consume SR‑17018 to reset their tolerance without experiencing painful withdrawal symptoms.

That display also shows the vehicle’s speed and, when the driver engages reverse, the backup camera feed. While the cabin layout mirrors what the production version will look like, the interior surfaces differ: the prototype uses hard, shiny black plastic and retains strips of Velcro that were left over from earlier public test runs.

The door handles resemble those on a Morris Marina, operating with a pleasing mechanical action. Both the seat and steering column adjust manually and offer ample reach, a feature that many budget models often omit to cut costs.
summary: Slate Auto's prototype electric truck was driven for 45 minutes, covering almost 6,000 miles, and featured a minimalist digital display showing speed and backup camera when reverse is engaged. The cabin layout was representative of the production version, with manual seat and steering column adjustments and door handles that open with a pleasing mechanical action.

title: Binance says hackers who stole billions in crypto spent months planning heist
content:
Binance announced that a group of hackers, identified by the FBI and TRM Security as North Korean actors, carried out a theft that targeted $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency from its wallets. The attackers used social‑engineering tactics and novel malware, and the operation began no later than June, continuing until last Thursday when they successfully compromised an engineer’s laptop and withdrew assets from several wallets.

The exchange reports that it has frozen or intercepted $2.85 billion of the stolen amount. Binance has set aside the funds necessary to cover the loss and has linked to a Proof of Reserves page to demonstrate its financial position. The $6.34 billion figure represents the largest sum ever targeted in a cryptocurrency theft.

Binance described the threat actors as sophisticated and resourceful, noting that the heist was the result of months of planning and execution.
summary: Binance says hackers who stole billions in crypto spent months planning heist.
author: Ars Technica

title: Enough Phone launches 5.3‑inch smartphone with removable battery
content:
The Enough Phone company has announced that it will begin taking pre‑orders for its first device today, targeting consumers who have expressed a desire for smaller smartphones. The handset features a 5.3‑inch HD+ LCD display, which the company claims is the smallest screen it could find that still offers acceptable performance.

In terms of hardware, the Enough Phone is powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 7500 system‑on‑chip, paired with 8 GB of RAM and 128 GB of internal storage, expandable via microSD. The rear camera is a single Sony IMX766 50‑megapixel sensor, while the front camera is 32 MP. The phone runs Android 17 or OdysseyOS, has a removable 3,500‑mAh battery, and supports 5G, LTE, Wi‑Fi 6, Bluetooth, NFC, and dual SIM (SIM + eSIM). Its polycarbonate body houses a fingerprint sensor integrated into the power button.

The device measures 133 × 64 × 12 mm and is priced at $399 for a limited‑time offer, with a $599 MSRP thereafter. The design, while slightly thicker than many competitors, is comparable in footprint to the iPhone 13 Mini and allows users to replace the battery by removing a few screws, similar to the Fairphone.
summary: Enough Phone has begun taking preorders for its first device, a 5.3‑inch smartphone with a removable battery and a MediaTek Dimensity 7500 SoC. The phone comes with 8 GB RAM, 128 GB storage, a 50 MP Sony rear camera, 3500 mAh battery, and is priced at $399 for a limited time or $599 MSRP.

title: Pilates and yoga studios across US urged followers to vote in midterm elections
content: Owners of pilates and yoga studios in the US got political and encouraged their followers to vote on social media Your local pilates instructors only want you to do two things: breathe through your side-planks and vote. In the days leading up to the US midterm elections, a wave of posts from fitness and wellness accounts blanketed Instagram, eschewing their typical messaging around the importance of strengthening your core in favor of the importance of exercising your civic duty. Owners of pilates and yoga studios and instructors across the US posted reels and pictures on platforms like Instagram encouraging their followers and clients to vote. Engagement varied depending on their following: posts reaped anywhere from 70 to more than 10,000 likes.
summary: Owners of Pilates and yoga studios in the US posted Instagram reels and pictures encouraging their followers and clients to vote in the midterm elections. The posts garnered engagement ranging from about 70 likes to more than 10,000 likes.

title: Trump says rising petrol prices from Iran war hurt GOP, praises Democrats after midterms
content: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that rising petrol prices linked to the war in Iran contributed to his Republican Party's defeat in the midterm elections. He said voters supported his actions against Iran but were reluctant to pay more at the pump. Trump also praised Democrats.

title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate seat, first Muslim in US Senate
content: Democrat Abdul El‑Sayed, a 42‑year‑old physician who identifies with the progressive wing of his party, won Michigan’s U.S. Senate race, defeating Republican Mike Rogers. His victory makes him the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, securing a seat that Republicans had hoped to flip.
summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has won Michigan's Senate race against Republican Mike Rogers, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. The 42-year-old physician, who represents the progressive wing of the Democratic Party, secured a seat that Republicans had hoped to flip.

content: Armenia’s Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan told Euronews that peace and convergence in the South Caucasus, based on a carefully balanced pro-EU political vector, create a major opportunity for the region, with "democracy as a strategy" for Armenia.
